narrative.overview:
DataHso feels like a compact route board installed at a guild archive: direct, sturdy, and built for repeated lookup. Saturated yellow gives destinations and selection an unmistakable signal; soot-black type, cool stone surroundings, white work surfaces, and hairline rules keep exact data ahead of ornament.

This is an operating interface, not a fantasy landing page or a generic analytics dashboard. Information density is deliberate, the first real records dominate the view, and identifiers remain visibly machine-readable. Pixel game art is contained and respected rather than enlarged into decoration.
keyCharacteristics: A yellow destination band acts as the signature wayfinding device.
Cool stone layers and white paper surfaces organize dense catalog data.
System sans typography carries prose; monospace carries IDs, codes, counts, and raw values.
Compact controls, 12–14px containers, and hairline borders create a precise instrument.
Motion confirms a route or panel transition without delaying lookup.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Direction Rule
rules.body: Use guild yellow for route-finding, selected destinations, and explicit state confirmation; do not wash ordinary cards or large content regions in it.

rules.name: The Semantic Colors Stay Semantic Rule
rules.body: Red, green, and focus blue communicate error, readiness, and keyboard focus respectively; they are not alternative brand accents.

rules.name: The Data Has Its Own Voice Rule
rules.body: Use monospace only where a value is copied, counted, coded, or structurally inspected; names and descriptions stay in system sans.

rules.name: The Records First Rule
rules.body: Do not insert a marketing hero between the route band, controls, and real records.

rules.name: The Horizontal Route Rule
rules.body: On constrained widths, preserve every destination in a touch- and keyboard-scrollable strip instead of collapsing routes into an opaque menu.

rules.name: The Structural Elevation Rule
rules.body: Use low shadow for grouping, stronger shadow for a surface that crosses the page plane, and never add decorative glow.

rules.name: The Selected Card Rule
rules.body: Selection is a 3px yellow halo plus an ink border; elevation alone must not carry selected state.

rules.name: The No Pills Rule
rules.body: Reserve circles for status; labels, actions, filters, and routes use compact rectangular silhouettes.

dos: Do use yellow to make destinations and selected states legible at a glance.
Do keep real records immediately below a compact control deck.
Do pair tonal layering with visible hairline borders so dense data remains structured without heavy shadow.
Do use monospace for IDs, codes, counts, metrics, and raw structured values.
Do preserve keyboard navigation, a 3px focus-blue outline, focus restoration, live status announcements, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do turn the right drawer into a bottom sheet at the mobile breakpoint.
donts: Don't introduce a decorative fantasy hero, parchment textures, ornamental medieval type, or generic dashboard chrome.
Don't use yellow as an all-purpose card background or red/green/blue as decorative accents.
Don't round controls into pills or erase the structural hairlines.
Don't smooth or upscale pixel game art beyond its contained media well.
Don't hide missing data or fabricate game values; use the established loading, waiting, empty, and error states.
Don't depend on motion alone to communicate route change, selection, loading, or panel state.
